_meta.description: Structural profile for RBI's Sectoral Deployment of Outstanding Credit by NBFCs (incl. HFCs), consumed by analysis/core/generate_skeleton.py. The simplest profile in the project: one statement, no reclassification lens, fifteen nodes, hierarchy entirely in the CSV's own parent_code column. The only authored input is the concept tag block.

columns.label: sector
columns.note_why: No `partition` and no `reclass_flag`. RBI publishes this as ONE statement, so a code alone identifies a row — unlike SIBC, where 2.3 is 'Large' in Statement 1 and 'Beverage and Tobacco' in Statement 2. And there is no memo lens re-slicing credit already counted, so every row belongs to the one tree.

period_selection.comment: Structure is taken from the latest DATA date. `release_date` is provenance, not structure — a later release can carry an older date's values without changing the shape.

exhaustive_decompositions.comment: The four 'of which' cuts, declared so the structural additivity check reports an EXPECTED residual instead of four permanent warnings — warnings nobody can act on are how a gate becomes noise. This is a second description of a fact the denominator rule measures every period, so it is GUARDED: test_nbfc_ingestion asserts the declaration matches what the compute finds.

signal_attach.comment: L1 signals carry compute.code as the entity identity key; this source has no partition to match on, so code alone resolves. Scan signals attach to the parent entity named by compute.parent_code.

concept.comment: COMPOSITION_SPEC.md §4 concept_tags. Tags MIRROR SIBC's on every overlapping entity — gold_loan is gold_loan in both books — because that shared vocabulary is what lets derive_cross_links propose the bank-vs-NBFC pairs later without a bespoke mapping table. The one tag that must NOT match is `lender`: SIBC is 'all' (the banking system), this is 'nbfc'. Without that distinction a cross-link would read bank housing credit and NBFC housing credit as the same rupees.
